review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it depends on in AlgorithmicSpec.lean (binaryListCode, rationalEntryBinaryCode, rationalMatrixBinaryCode). I grepped downstream uses of the wrapper definitions (machineListHead, machineListTail, machineMatrixRowsWord, and the others) across LeanPool/BeyondBethe. I read the call sites in MachineKuhnRunner, MachineOptimizerMatrixBitBound and MachineRationalVectorSum. I did not run Lean. The suggestions are untested, and I don't claim any simp failure was observed. The wrappers are plain, non-reducible defs, so they do not unfold during simp. The existing `_cons` and `_encode` lemmas are stated at the code-constructor level (`binaryListCode _ (x :: xs)`, `rationalEntryBinaryCode q`, `rationalMatrixBinaryEncoding.encode`). Because of that, the interface breaks once a caller's simp set also unfolds `binaryListCode`. I found no loop, competing-rule or orientation problems.

findings.declaration: machineListHead_cons / machineListTail_cons (missing pair-level simp lemmas for machineListHead / machineListTail)
findings.excerpt:
machineListHead (binaryListCode encode (x :: xs)) = encode x := by
  simp [machineListHead, binaryListCode]
findings.problem: The only simp lemmas for `machineListHead` and `machineListTail` are keyed on `binaryListCode encode (x :: xs)`. The wrappers are non-reducible defs, so `machinePairFirst_pair` and `machinePairSecond_pair` do not fire on `machineListHead (pair a b)`. Callers already simp with `binaryListCode` unfolded. That turns the argument into `pair (encode x) (binaryListCode encode xs)` before `machineListHead_cons` can match. They then have to add `machineListHead, machineListTail` to the simp set to expose the pair lemmas, for example in MachineKuhnRunner (`binaryListCode, machineKuhnStackPush, List.finRange_succ, machineListHead, machineListTail`) and MachineOptimizerMatrixBitBound (`matrixEntryLengthSemCode, machineListHead, machineListTail`). Unfolding the wrappers leaks the implementation `machinePairFirst`/`machinePairSecond`, which this file was meant to hide.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem machineListHead_pair (left right : List Bool) : machineListHead (pair left right) = left := machinePairFirst_pair left right` and the matching `machineListTail_pair` for `machinePairSecond_pair`. Keep the `_cons` lemmas and define them via these pair lemmas. Do the same for the other wrappers (`machineMatrixDimensionWord_pair`, `machineMatrixRowsWord_pair`, `machineRationalEntryNumeratorWord_pair`, `machineRationalEntryDenominatorWord_pair`). Callers can then drop the unfold lemmas for the wrappers from their simp sets.
findings.benefit: Simp normalizes `machineListHead`/`machineListTail` applied to a `pair` whether or not `binaryListCode` has been unfolded. Downstream simp calls no longer need to unfold the wrapper definitions, and the interface stays abstract.

findings.declaration: machineMatrixDimensionWord_encode / machineMatrixRowsWord_encode (no simp lemmas for machineMatrixDimensionWord / machineMatrixRowsWord on a `pair`)
findings.problem: Both `machineMatrixDimensionWord` and `machineMatrixRowsWord` are non-reducible defs. Their only simp lemmas are stated on `rationalMatrixBinaryEncoding.encode ⟨n, A⟩`, a projection of a structure constant. After a caller unfolds the code to `pair n.bits (binaryListCode …)`, or when the argument is a general `pair` such as one produced by `machineMatrixRowsWord (machineRowUpperMatrixWord word)`, no simp lemma applies. Callers end up unfolding the wrapper by hand, as in MachineRationalVectorSum: `simp [machineMatrixRawSumInit, …, binaryListCode, machineMatrixRowsWord]`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem machineMatrixDimensionWord_pair (l r : List Bool) : machineMatrixDimensionWord (pair l r) = l` and `@[simp] theorem machineMatrixRowsWord_pair (l r : List Bool) : machineMatrixRowsWord (pair l r) = r`, proved from `machinePairFirst_pair`/`machinePairSecond_pair`. Consider also stating the `_encode` lemmas for `rationalMatrixBinaryCode ⟨n, A⟩`, which is the form `AlgorithmicSpec` uses in `F (rationalMatrixBinaryCode x) = …`. They would then fire without going through `rationalMatrixBinaryEncoding.encode`.
findings.benefit: The simp interface for the matrix accessors is complete on both the abstract `pair` form and the concrete code form. Proofs can stop unfolding `machineMatrixRowsWord` and `machineMatrixDimensionWord`.
